text:
incidents-bot: P1 alert — elevated websocket/streaming timeouts observed for MeridianBank (VPC gateway route meridian-prod). Summary: 502s and abrupt ws closes from 21:03–21:09 UTC, multiple customer sessions impacted. Paging @sre-oncall and @eng-runtime-lead.

sre-oncall: Ack — I'm on. Can we confirm customer impact surface? Is this tenant-scoped?

jessica: Looks tenant-scoped to Meridian only. Traffic spike to meridian-dedicated-1 at 21:02, backend app-gw started returning ECONNRESET during frame writes. Example from gateway logs: 
```
2026-03-17T21:04:12Z WARN ws_conn.go:214 write failed: write tcp 10.12.4.5:443->172.31.9.12:52344: write: connection reset by peer
```

pablo: Network telemetry shows burst of TCP RSTs between our gateway egress and Meridian app-gw IPs; TLS handshakes complete, so not cert-related. No obvious infra CPU/IO saturation on our side.

kwon: Mitigation plan: 1) Increase upstream idle timeout and keepalive on Meridian route to account for upstream proxy behavior, 2) shift 20% traffic to meridian-dedicated-2 as a soft fallback, 3) enable shorter retry window on client-facing gateway to avoid thundering retries. Applying step 1 now to edge-3 and edge-4.

maya-solutions: Customer reported JS error "websocket: close 1006" and is asking for ETA. I'll let them know we have a mitigation in flight. Can you confirm whether this will cause session loss?

jessica: Increasing keepalive/idle should reduce mid-stream EOFs; there may be some transient session drops during routing changes. We'll try to move traffic gradually to avoid mass reconnections.

eng-runtime-lead: Commands I'm running: 
```
# quick rollout via rctl
rctl route update meridian-prod --keepalive=90s --upstream-idle-timeout=120s
rctl route canary meridian-prod --target-pool meridian-dedicated-2 --traffic-shift 20 --duration 2m
```

pablo: Deployed config to edge-3 -> logs show fewer RSTs within 30s. Initiating the 20% canary shift now.

incidents-bot: Note: oncall escalation timer set — auto-escalate to eng-paging if unresolved in 15m.

kwon: Observability update: 21:07 -> ws timeout rate down 60% on meridian route, 502s trending down. Still seeing occasional client reconnects.

maya-solutions: Messaging Meridian-CX: "We've applied routing and keepalive changes; you may see brief reconnects. Please report any persistent 1006s." :email: 

jessica: Quick snippet of the temporary nginx upstream patch we used (for records):
```
upstream meridian_backend {
  server 10.12.9.5:443;
  keepalive 100;
  keepalive_requests 1000;
}
proxy_read_timeout 120s;
proxy_send_timeout 120s;
```

eng-runtime-lead: Canary completed, fallback pool handling looks healthy. Metrics: active streams stable, p95 latency back to baseline.

pablo: Rolling the idle/keepalive to remaining edges (edge-1, edge-2) now for completeness.

kwon: Confirming tenant isolation: only Meridian affected, no bleed to other tenants. Good.

incidents-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation in progress, doc created at /incidents/4159876543.

maya-solutions: Customer confirmed fewer failures and will stand by for 30m. I'll log the customer update in the incident doc. :white_check_mark: 

sre-oncall: Leaving note — we'll keep this open for monitoring window (2h). Postmortem required to understand root cause (likely upstream app-gw connection handling). If anything degrades, escalate immediately.

eng-runtime-lead: Agreed. Follow-ups: capture full tcpdump for meridian IP pair, ask customer for proxy config (idle/keepalive), and evaluate long-term routing policy (pin to dedicated spare or connection rewriter).

incidents-bot: Thread closed for now — last update at 21:18 UTC."
